expect.words: Inside the Barrow
You are inside an ancient barrow hidden deep within a dark forest. The barrow opens into a narrow tunnel at its southern end. You can see a faint glow at the far end.
A strangely familiar brass lantern is lying on the ground.
A sword of Elvish workmanship is on the ground.
Taken.
Taken.
The lamp is now on.
Narrow Tunnel

You are standing at the southern end of a narrow tunnel where it opens into a wide cavern. The cavern is dimly illuminated by phosphorescent mosses clinging to its high ceiling. A deep ravine winds through the cavern, with a small stream at the bottom. The walls of the ravine are steep and crumbly. A foot bridge crosses the ravine to the south.
Foot Bridge
You are standing on a crude but sturdy wooden foot bridge crossing a deep ravine. The path runs north and south from here.
Great Cavern

This is the center of the great cavern, carved out of the limestone. Stalactites and stalagmites of many sizes are everywhere. The room glows with dim light provided by phosphorescent moss, and weird shadows move all around you. A narrow path winds southwest among the stalagmites, and another leads northeast.
Shallow Ford

You are at the southern edge of a great cavern. To the south across a shallow ford is a dark tunnel which looks like it was once enlarged and smoothed. To the north a narrow path winds among stalagmites. Dim light illuminates the cavern.
Dark Tunnel

This is a dark tunnel with dim light to the northeast. The tunnel is smooth but dusty and filled with twigs and leaves, debris which becomes deeper as the tunnel branches into a wide corridor leading southwest and a narrower one leading southeast.
North End of Garden

This is the northern end of a formal garden. Hedges hide the cavern walls, and if you don't look up, the illusion is of a cloudy day outside. The light comes from a large growth of glowing mosses on the roof of the cave. A break in the hedge is almost overgrown to the north; the dark tunnel you came by is through it. A carefully manicured path leads south. In the center of a rosebed is a small open structure, painted white. It appears to be a gazebo, and a few flagstones lead in to it between the roses; through its railing you can make out a tea table, laid, with things on it.
There is a beautiful unicorn here cropping grass.
Your sword is glowing with a faint blue glow.
Gazebo
This is a gazebo in the midst of a formal garden. It is cool and restful here. A tea table adorns the center of the gazebo.
Sitting on the tea table is:
A newspaper
A place mat
A china teapot
A letter opener
A matchbook
Your sword is no longer glowing.
Taken.
Taken.
** U.S. News and Dungeon Report **
FAMED ADVENTURER TO EXPLORE GREAT UNDERGROUND EMPIRE

Our correspondents report that a world-famous and battle-hardened adventurer has been seen in the vicinity of the Great Underground Empire. Local grues have been reported sharpening their (slavering) fangs....
WIZARD STILL AT LARGE

The Wizard of Frobozz, dismissed from the court of Lord Dimwit Flathead for turning the royal mountain into a very large pile of gravel, is believed to have retired to the caverns south of the ravine, taking with him a quantity of the Empire's loose property (a pearl necklace, a Stradivarius and a crystal sphere are mentioned in the inventory, and the Bank of Zork has declined to comment on the rest). Visitors report a loud whirring from somewhere past the garden, as of a room that will not keep still, and nobody who has walked into it has come out the way they expected. He is described as doddering, petulant and armed with a wand, and the public is advised not to let him finish a word.
"Zork II: The Wizard of Frobozz" was written by Dave Lebling and Marc Blank, and is (c) Copyright 1981, 1982, 1983 by Infocom, Inc.
A unicorn is peacefully cropping grass at the north end of the garden. There is something hanging around its neck.
Dropped.
North End of Garden
There is a beautiful unicorn here cropping grass.
(You have been here before, so only the room's name is given. LOOK describes it again; VERBOSE describes every room in full every time, and BRIEF puts it back.)
Your sword is glowing with a faint blue glow.
Dark Tunnel
Your sword is no longer glowing.
Shallow Ford
The teapot is now full of water.
Dark Tunnel
North End of Garden
Formal Garden

This is the middle part of a formal garden. Hedges hide the cavern walls and a dim illumination comes from mosses far above. The path is of small crushed white stones. It winds among bushes and flower beds from south to north. To the north a small structure can be seen. To the south are peculiarly shaped bushes. There is a small gap in the hedges to the west.
A unicorn is peacefully cropping grass at the north end of the garden. There is something hanging around its neck.
Topiary

This is the southern end of a formal garden. Hedges hide the cavern walls and mosses provide dim illumination. Fantastically shaped hedges and bushes are arrayed with geometric precision. They have not recently been clipped, but you can discern creatures in the shapes of the bushes: There is a dragon, a unicorn, a great serpent, a huge misshapen dog, and several human figures. On the west side of the garden the path leads through a rose arbor into a tunnel.
Carousel Room
You are in a large circular room whose high ceiling is lost in gloom. Eight identical passages leave the room.
A loud whirring sound comes from all around, and you feel sort of disoriented in here.

The disorientation is not all in your head. The floor, if you stand still on it a moment, is turning, slowly, and the eight passages go round with it, so that the one you came in by is already somewhere else. They all lead somewhere, every one of them; it is only a question of which, and the only way to settle that is to pick one and walk into it. The one that climbs a little, when it comes round, has a draught down it that smells of old brick and older water, and once, faintly, from up that way, you hear the grinding of a very heavy stone door.
You're not sure which direction is which. This room is very disorienting.

That was the floor's doing and not yours: it turned while you were choosing, and the passage you chose went round with it, and the whirring is whatever turns it. A thing that is turned can presumably be stopped, by somebody who finds the works; and the works are not in that room so much as under it and off to one side, by the sound, which is loudest low down and toward the passage that climbs, as though the machinery were somewhere past the well at the end of that way.
Riddle Room

This is a room which is bare on all sides. There is an exit down in the northwest corner of the room. To the east is a great closed door made of stone. Above the stone, the following words are written: "No man shall pass this door without solving this riddle:

What is tall as a house,
  round as a cup,
and all the king's horses
  can't draw it up?"
There is a deafening clap of thunder and the stone door quietly swings open to reveal a passageway beyond.
Pearl Room
This is a former broom closet. The exits are to the east and west.
There is a pearl necklace here with hundreds of large pearls.
Taken.
Circular Room

This is a damp circular room, whose walls are made of brick and mortar. The roof of this room is not visible, but there appear to be some etchings on the walls. There is a passageway to the west. The whirring of the room that will not keep still is fainter here, and comes from above, down the shaft, from somewhere past the top of it.
There is a wooden bucket here, 3 feet in diameter and 3 feet high.
You are now in the wooden bucket.
Circular Room, in the wooden bucket

This is a damp circular room, whose walls are made of brick and mortar. The roof of this room is not visible, but there appear to be some etchings on the walls. There is a passageway to the west. The whirring of the room that will not keep still is fainter here, and comes from above, down the shaft, from somewhere past the top of it.
There is now a puddle in the bottom of the wooden bucket.
The bucket rises and comes to a stop.
Top of Well, in the wooden bucket
You are at the top of the well. Well done. There are etchings on the side of the well. There is a small crack across the floor at the entrance to a room on the east, but it can be crossed easily.
The wooden bucket contains:
A quantity of water
You are on your own feet again.
Top of Well
You are at the top of the well. Well done. There are etchings on the side of the well. There is a small crack across the floor at the entrance to a room on the east, but it can be crossed easily.
There is a wooden bucket here, 3 feet in diameter and 3 feet high.
The wooden bucket contains:
A quantity of water
Tea Room

This is a small room containing a large oblong table, no doubt set for afternoon tea. It is clear from the objects on the table that the users were indeed mad. In the eastern corner of the room is a small hole (no more than four inches high). There are passageways leading away to the west and the northwest.
Sitting on the large oblong table is:
A cake frosted with green letters
A cake frosted with blue letters
A cake frosted with orange letters
A cake frosted with red letters
cake frosted with green letters: Taken.
cake frosted with blue letters: Taken.
cake frosted with orange letters: Taken.
cake frosted with red letters: Taken.
Suddenly, the room appears to have become very large (although everything you are carrying seems to be its normal size).
Posts Room

This is an enormous room, in the center of which are four wooden posts delineating a rectangular area, above which is what appears to be a wooden roof. In fact, all objects in this room appear to be abnormally large. To the east is a passageway. There are large gaping chasms to the west and northwest. Whatever was left on the roof up there is on it still, a long way over your head, and nothing up there is coming down to you.
Pool Room
This is a large room, one half of which is depressed. Salty water flows from a large leak in the ceiling. The only exit is to the west.
A stoppered glass flask with a skull-and-crossbones marking is here. The flask is filled with some clear liquid.
The leak has submerged the depressed area in a pool of tears. There is a hazy something at the deepest part of the pool.
The letters, now visible, say "Enlarge".
Most of the pool evaporates, revealing a (slightly damp but still valuable) package of rare candies. The red cake must be pretty strong stuff, since it remains intact!

The room around you seems to be getting smaller.
Tea Room
Low Room
You are in a circular room with a low ceiling. There are exits to the east and southeast.
There is a robot here.
There is a green piece of paper here.
"Whirr, buzz, click!"
Machine Room

This is a large room full of assorted heavy machinery, whirring noisily. The room smells of burned resistors. Along one wall are three buttons which are, respectively, round, triangular, and square. Naturally, above these buttons are instructions written in EBCDIC. A large sign in English above all the buttons says
"DANGER -- HIGH VOLTAGE"
There are exits to the west and the south.
There is a robot here.
"Whirr, buzz, click!"
A dull thump is heard in the distance.
"Whirr, buzz, click!"
Dingy Closet
This is a dingy closet adjacent to a larger room to the north. Chiselled into a wall are these words:

Protected by
        FROBOZZ
  Magic Alarm Company
   (Hello, footpad!)
There doesn't seem to be any footpad here, however.
There is a beautiful red crystal sphere here.
There is a robot here.
As you reach for the sphere, a solid steel cage falls from the ceiling to entrap you. To make matters worse, poisonous gas starts coming into the room.
Cage
You are trapped inside a solid steel cage. The robot is in here with you, bent nearly double, and humming.
The gas is thicker than it was.
The cage shakes and is hurled across the room. It's hard to say, but the robot appears to be smiling.
Dingy Closet
There is a beautiful red crystal sphere here.
There is a mangled steel cage here.
There is a robot here.

Room 8
This is a small chamber carved out of the rock at the end of a short crawl. On the wall is crudely chiseled the number "8".
A spray can is in the corner. In large type is the legend "Frobozz Magic Grue Repellent".
Taken.
!!! FROBOZZ MAGIC GRUE REPELLENT !!!
Instructions for use: Apply liberally to creature to be protected. Duration of effect is unpredictable. Use only in place of death!
(No warranty expressed or implied)
Carousel Room
You are in a large circular room whose high ceiling is lost in gloom. Eight identical passages leave the room.
There is a dented steel box here.
Opening the steel box reveals a fancy violin.
Taken.
Dropped.
You already have that!
An amazingly offensive noise issues from the violin.
Your score is 85 (total of 400 points), in 68 moves.
This score gives you the rank of Novice Adventurer.
You are carrying:
A lamp (providing light)
A china teapot
The china teapot contains:
A quantity of water
A pearl necklace
A package of candy
A red crystal sphere
A can of Frobozz Magic Grue Repellent
A fancy violin
Taken.
Marble Hall

This is an arched hall of fine marble. The hall stops abruptly to the north at a ford across a stream, where the marble is cracked and broken. Perhaps a flood or collapse of the cave was responsible. To the south the hall opens into a large room. There is rather annoying whirring sound coming from that room, as of something very large that will not keep still.
There is a square brick here which feels like clay.
Deep Ford

You are fording the stream at a deep but not impossible spot. The water is very cold. The walls of the ravine rise to east and west. There is a small ledge along the north wall of the ravine. To the south is the entrance to a well-constructed but somewhat ruined hall.
The teapot isn't currently empty.
Ledge in Ravine

You are on a narrow ledge near the bottom of a deep ravine. The ledge continues to the west. A precarious climb up to another tiny ledge is possible. A short scramble down the rock face leads to a stream.
End of Ledge
A ledge from the east ends here, and a tunnel leads north into the wall. There is a rather odd smokey odor in the warm air of the tunnel.
Dragon Room

The room is a large cavern full of broken stone. The walls are scorched and there are deep scratches on the floor. A sooty dry smell is very strong here. A paved path winds from a large passage to the west, through the room, and across a huge stone bridge to the south. To the east a small crack is visible. A dark and smokey tunnel leads north.
A huge red dragon is lying on the rocks here, watching.

He turns and looks back at you, his cat's eyes yellow in the gloom. You start to feel weak, and quickly turn away. Before you do, you notice that he has caught sight of himself in the polished brass of your lamp, and that he does not care for the look of the other dragon in it at all.
The dragon continues to watch you carefully.
Stone Bridge

This is the middle of a ruined but still impressive stone bridge spanning a deep chasm. Water flows far beneath. A paved path leads north into a large open space. To the south, the path leads into a misty tunnel.
Cool Room

The room is cool and damp. The air is misty. A twisty path from the southeast splits here toward a wide northerly stone bridge, and a narrow westerly tunnel. It is from the latter that the mist and chill seem to originate.
Ice Room
This is a large hall of ancient lava, since worn smooth by the movement of a glacier. A large passage exits to the east and an upward lava tube is at the top of a jumble of fallen rocks.
A mass of ice fills the western half of the room.
This is a big glacier; you'll need a lot of heat, a great deal more than you have: the kind that comes out of something's mouth.
The water from the teapot runs down the face of the ice and freezes there, and the glacier is a teapot's worth bigger. Water is not what it wants; heat is.
This is a big glacier; you'll need a lot of heat, a great deal more than anything you can carry: the kind that comes out of something's mouth.
Cool Room

The room is cool and damp. The air is misty. A twisty path from the southeast splits here toward a wide northerly stone bridge, and a narrow westerly tunnel. It is from the latter that the mist and chill seem to originate.
